reason: CSP with 'unsafe-inline' for scripts and styles: Next.js hydrates the page with inline scripts, next-themes sets the theme with one and the accent colour is an inline style. A nonce would need every page rendered per request. The rest of the policy (no framing, no plugins, same-origin connections, a fixed list of image hosts and form targets) is what protects the interface; see src/lib/security-headers.ts.

A form that is a server action carries no CSRF token: Next.js refuses an action called from another origin and a form cannot set the header an action needs. The csrf suite of qa/security plays this against the real image (another site, a plain form on another site, null origin) and checks that nothing changes.

SQL injection reported on the forms that are server actions (every field of the event form, and the internal fields of the action, $ACTION_REF_1 and $ACTION_1:0). The rule compares the page for a condition that is true and one that is false, with no evidence of its own (the report has an empty evidence and medium confidence), and the answer of a server action carries data that changes from one call to the next. Nothing in src/ builds SQL from a string (Prisma binds every value, qa-rules forbids the rest), and the sql suite of qa/security plays the same pairs, and hostile statements, against the real image in every string, number and boolean of the arguments of EVERY server action (the cases of the access matrix, so a new action is attacked without anybody listing it): the outcome never depends on whether the condition is true, and no table changes that the action does not change. The entry accepts the rule ONLY where the suite attacked ("proven": the page must hold an attacked action and the field be one it was attacked through, sql-proven.ts and zap-gate.mjs): an alert anywhere else fails the job.
